newsitem.title: DENMARK: FORECAST-Danish employers raise growth forecast.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Danish employers raise growth forecast.

text.p: The Danish Confederation of Industry on Tuesday revised upward its forecasts for 1996 and 1997 GDP growth and predicted an increased current account surplus, but left its expectations for 1996 inflation unchanged.
The Confederation's revised survey saw growth of 2.2 percent in 1996 and 2.5 percent in 1997 compared with its June forecast of 0.9 percent in 1996 and 2.0 percent next year.

It said the current account, 16 billion crowns in surplus at the end of August, was expected to end 1996 with a 12 billion crown surplus, after overseas interest payments falling due at year-end. Its June assessment saw a 10 billion crown surplus.
The new forecast held to an earlier prediction of 2.1 percent inflation in 1996 but raised expectations for 1997 consumer prices to a 2.3 percent rise, from its earlier 2.0 percent.
It saw 1996 unemployment at around 245,000, falling to 232,000 in 1997 and and 227,000 in 1998.
Official figures put 1995 unemployment at 288,400. Unemployment in September this year was 234,700 or 8.4 percent of the workforce.
